# AGENTS.md — 13-fashion-lookbook

Instructions for AI coding agents working in this folder.

## Context
- Template: **OSTEN**, fashion brand, style "35mm contact sheet on a light table".
- Stack: Next.js 16, TypeScript, plain CSS. Do not add dependencies unless the user asks.
- The design contract is in `DESIGN.md`. Read it before changing anything visual.

## Files
- `lib/content.ts` — rolls, frames (Unsplash ids, select/reject), all copy (EN + RU)
- `app/page.tsx` — page, contact strips, loupe
- `app/globals.css` — tokens and film/loupe styles
- `app/layout.tsx` — fonts and metadata

## How to run
- `npm install`
- `npm run dev`
- `npm run build   # static export to ./out`

## Rules
- Content changes go to the content file, not into markup or components.
- Every user-facing string exists in **en** and **ru**. English is the default; `?lang=ru` and the language button switch it.
- Colors, fonts, radii and spacing are tokens. Change tokens, not individual elements.
- Keep the signature block: Lookbook as film contact sheets: black-and-white frames, grease-pencil circles on selects, crosses on rejects, a round loupe that shows the frame in colour.
- Keep accessibility: semantic headings, visible focus, alt text, `prefers-reduced-motion` support, body text contrast ≥ 4.5:1.
- Keep it static: no backend, no booking or payment flows.
- Frames are grayscale on the sheet and colour only on hover or in the loupe.
- Red is only grease pencil; orange is only film edge print.
- Prata for titles and looks, Tenor Sans in spaced capitals for UI.
- Marks are SVG paths; selects and rejects are data flags in content.ts.
- No prices, no cart — it's a lookbook.

## Done means
- The page builds/opens without console errors.
- Both languages render with no missing strings.
- Layout works from 360 px to 1920 px wide.
